title: Ola Electric Hands Sales to Dealers as Registrations Fall 19.5% in September Quarter
excerpt: The company that built its name on direct-to-consumer stores has appointed 255 dealer partners running 319 stores, targets about 700 by March 2027, and stopped taking orders through its own stores on November 1.
body:
• Ola Electric's vehicle registrations fell 19.5% year-on-year to 41,653 units in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and were down 5.3% sequentially.
  • The company reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 362 crore for the quarter — narrower than a year earlier, wider than the previous quarter.
  • As of November 8, Ola had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores, and plans about 450 stores by December 2026 and around 700 by March 2027. It stopped accepting orders through its own direct-to-consumer stores on November 1.
  • Founder Bhavish Aggarwal told the earnings call "demand is no longer our constraint," blaming supply-chain capacity for delayed deliveries, including about 5,000 paid orders held up in September for want of chargers.

Ola Electric built its brand by refusing to use dealers. It is now handing its showrooms to them.

On the earnings call for the July-September quarter of FY27, founder Bhavish Aggarwal reiterated one phrase: "Demand is no longer our constraint." The claim sits awkwardly next to the quarter's own numbers. Registrations fell 19.5% year-on-year to 41,653 units in the quarter ended September 30 and slipped 5.3% from the previous quarter, The Morning Context reported, and the company is raising money once again.

What the dealer model changes

The mechanics explain the pivot. Under Ola's company-owned retail model, the manufacturer financed the inventory sitting in its own stores. Under the dealer model, dealers pay for vehicles when they order them and hold the stock themselves — moving the working-capital burden off Ola's balance sheet. Channel inventory was approximately 15 days, the company said, with some of its earliest dealer locations holding less than a week's stock.

As of November 8, the company had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores, Lapaas Voice's earnings summary reported. It plans about 450 stores by December 2026 and around 700 by March 2027, expects closing most company-operated stores to save approximately Rs 50 crore in operating expenses, and stopped accepting orders through its own stores on November 1. The dealer rollout began in September across seven states — Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Bihar, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh — after the company said it received more than 1,200 expressions of interest from prospective partners, Inc42 reported.

The supply story management is telling

Aggarwal attributed the shortfall to supply, not buyers: supplier capacity and component availability, rather than factory capacity, limited deliveries. About 5,000 vehicles with paid orders in September were delayed by roughly a week into October because chargers were unavailable, the company said, and it is targeting production of approximately 25,000 vehicles in December 2026 as the backlog clears.

The balance sheet has been repaired in parallel. Total borrowings declined to Rs 1,819 crore in September 2026 from Rs 3,132 crore in December 2024, and the September-quarter net loss of Rs 362 crore was narrower than a year earlier, though wider than the June quarter.

What to watch

Dealers solve distribution; they do not by themselves solve the service complaints that dogged Ola's direct model. Under the new arrangement, dealer partners handle local sales and service and hold spare-parts inventory locally — the test is whether turnaround times, which the company said fell from about nine days in October 2025 to nearly one day in March 2026, hold up as the network triples in size by March 2027.
